title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026

claims.claim: $11.66B in unobligated Inflation Reduction Act education funds rescinded (Sec. 528)
claims.sourceSpan: Sec. 528. Of the unobligated balances of amounts made available in section 10301(1)(A)(iii) of Public Law 117-169, $11,661,000,000 are hereby rescinded.
claims.note: Right-fact-wrong-actor. The $11.661B rescission is real and cited to Sec. 528, but the funds are NOT education funds. Sec. 528 sits in Division B's cross-departmental Title V general provisions (its neighbors are Sec. 527 = CHIP Child Enrollment Contingency Fund and Sec. 529 = ACF/BLS), not the Education title. The cited source — section 10301(1)(A)(iii) of PL 117-169 — is the Inflation Reduction Act's 'Enhancement of Internal Revenue Service Resources' appropriation (IRS operations funding), not education spending. The word 'education' appears nowhere in the source provision.

claims.claim: rescinding $11.66B in IRA education funds / 'Reduces previously enacted education spending by $11.66B'
claims.sourceSpan: Sec. 528. Of the unobligated balances of amounts made available in section 10301(1)(A)(iii) of Public Law 117-169, $11,661,000,000 are hereby rescinded.
claims.note: Division-layer restatement of the same misattribution: characterizes the Sec. 528 rescission of PL 117-169 sec. 10301(1)(A)(iii) balances as 'education spending authority.' Source cites IRA IRS-enhancement funding; no education account or the word 'education' is present in the provision, which is a Division B Title V general provision spanning Labor/HHS/Education, not an Education-title cut.

claims.claim: Funds the SBA's loan guarantee programs ($35.5B 7(a), $15B disaster, $6B SBIC debentures)
claims.sourceSpan: during fiscal year 2026, guarantees of trust certificates authorized by section 5(g) of the Small Business Act shall not exceed a principal amount of $15,000,000,000. [disaster loans program account] To carry out the direct loan program authorized by section 7(b) of the Small Business Act, $282,000,000
claims.note: Right-fact-wrong-actor. The $15B figure is the 7(a) TRUST-CERTIFICATE guarantee ceiling under Sec. 5(g) of the Small Business Act — not disaster loans. SBA disaster loans are appropriated at $282M (direct loan program, section 7(b)). The '$15B disaster' label binds the correct number to the wrong account.

claims.field: divisions[3].brief (recurs: divisions[3].gaps[1]; top-level gaps 'SBA disaster loan ceiling of $15B')
claims.claim: the SBA is authorized for $35.5B in business loan guarantees and $15B in disaster loans
claims.sourceSpan: guarantees of trust certificates authorized by section 5(g) of the Small Business Act shall not exceed a principal amount of $15,000,000,000 ... To carry out the direct loan program authorized by section 7(b) of the Small Business Act, $282,000,000
claims.note: Same misattribution at the division layer. $15B is the 7(a) trust-certificate guarantee ceiling (Sec. 5(g)); SBA disaster lending is $282M direct (section 7(b)). Division E's own top_lines correctly label $15B as the '7(a) trust certificate guarantee ceiling' and disaster as '$282M', so the brief/gaps contradict the top_lines and misstate the source.

claims.field: summary (recurs: top_lines[6].headline 'Division H — DHS Continuing Resolution' & subs; divisions[6].label/summary/brief/top_lines)
claims.claim: DHS funded at FY2025 enacted levels through February 13, 2026 under Public Law 119-37
claims.sourceSpan: Sec. 101. The Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026 (division A of Public Law 119-37) is amended by striking the date specified in section 106(3) and inserting ``February 13, 2026''. [Secs. 102-105 contain no reference to the Department of Homeland Security or DHS]
claims.note: Division H's text names no agency. It is a general extension of the PL 119-37 continuing resolution (amends the date in sec. 106(3) to Feb 13, 2026) plus lapse ratification/back-pay provisions covering every account funded under that CR — not DHS specifically. The DHS-specific attribution is nowhere in the fetched Division H source; the analysis's own summary also says the Act funds only 'five of the twelve' regular bills, which implies multiple agencies (not just DHS) remain under the CR.

claims.claim: SBIC debenture guarantee ceiling: $6B; SBIC equity guarantee ceiling: $16.5B
claims.sourceSpan: commitments to guarantee loans under section 503 of the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 and commitments for loans authorized under subparagraph (C) of section 502(7) ... shall not exceed, in the aggregate, $16,500,000,000
claims.note: The $16.5B ceiling is for commitments under section 503 and section 502(7) of the Small Business Investment Act (Certified Development Company / 504 debenture program), not 'SBIC equity.' The $6B SBIC-debenture figure (section 303(b)) is correct; the $16.5B is mislabeled.
